editorial:
Imagine a dad who spends his whole life bragging about how open-minded he is. He tells everyone he hates discrimination and loves equality, but all that talk goes out the window the second his son tells him he is marrying another man. You get to watch this guy completely flip-flop from being a liberal hero to a stressed-out mess who will do anything to stop the wedding. It is a loud, chaotic, and funny look at how people act when their beliefs are actually put to the test in their own living room.

The acting is great because the lead captures that frantic energy perfectly, making the embarrassing moments feel real. While the plot follows a pretty standard comedy path, the chemistry between the family members keeps you interested. It is a lighthearted ride, though some jokes might feel a bit repetitive. If you are in the mood for something feel-good, you should definitely check it out.
endingExplained: After a lot of fighting and funny mishaps, the father finally realizes that his love for his son is more important than his stubborn pride. He stops trying to ruin the party and fully accepts the couple. The movie wraps up with a beautiful, heartfelt wedding ceremony where the dad gives his blessing. It ends on a high note, showing that true tolerance comes from love, not just saying the right words in public.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family comedies with a sweet message.
